evidence: Ter. And. 903: Prō peccātō magnō paulum supplicī satis est patrī
terms.comment: A fault, a wrong; in the Church, a sin (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Par. 3.20: peccāre est tamquam trānsilīre līneās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To do wrong, to sin; against someone, in aliquem (peccāvī in caelum, Lc. 15.21).

phrases.latin: Pater, peccāvī in caelum, et cōram tē: jam nōn sum dignus vocārī fīlius tuus.
phrases.english: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.

phrases.latin: Quid fēcī? quid commeruī aut peccāvī, pater?
phrases.english: What have I done? What have I deserved, what wrong have I done, father?
such a little boy and such a great sinner
God, be merciful to me, a sinner.

sources: Lewis & Short: peccatum · Lewis & Short: pecco · Lewis & Short: peccator
